edits.value_json: 四 means ‘four.’ Its present form has enclosing 囗 strokes around inner 儿-form strokes. One account describes Shang 亖 as four strokes used directly for ‘four’; the origin of 四 remains disputed. Proposals treat 四 as a breath-related graph for 呬, later borrowed for ‘four’, or as the original graph of 泗 depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; the latter proposal lacks textual attestation.

The current graph has enclosing 囗 strokes around inner strokes; this modern description does not establish the ancient identities or roles of those shapes. Ancient analyses remain disputed. One interprets four horizontal marks as counting rods representing four. Another proposes that 四 was a graph for 呬 depicting breath, later reused for ‘four’ because of sound similarity; the proposed breath-related referent’s original name is not independently established. A separate proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; this proposal lacks textual attestation. Neither borrowing account is established.
